texts.orig: Subject: Licensing of owners in Thoroughbred racing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Purpose: To establish criteria for licensing horse owners in Thorougbred racing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Text of proposed rule: § 4026.3. Nonmanaging ownership.
texts.text: Text of proposed rule: § 4026.3. Nonmanaging ownership.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: (b) Nonmanaging owners-licensing. No horse shall be entered or started by such horse's managing owner that is owned by [35] 20 or [less] fewer owners, unless all of the owners are licensed, or, if owned by more than [35] 20 owners, unless each individual having a [three] five percent or greater property interest is licensed as an owner by the commission. In addition, each such owner that is not an individual must be registered and licensed with the commission, and all such entity's officers, directors, trustees or other managing individuals must be licensed by the commission unless otherwise directed by the commission. The commission may also require any other individual involved in ownership to be licensed at any time [it] the commission may deem desirable. The commission or the State steward, for good cause, may waive any of such requirements for a race. In no event, however, may a horse start, if the license of any such individual has been denied, suspended or revoked, until the commission is satisfied that any withdrawal of such individual or transfer of such individual's interest is in good faith.

texts.orig: 2. LEGISLATIVE OBJECTIVES: To enable the Commission to enhance the integrity and safety of Thoroughbred horse racing and generate reasonable revenue for the support of government.
texts.text: LEGISLATIVE OBJECTIVES: To enable the Commission to enhance the integrity and safety of Thoroughbred horse racing and generate reasonable revenue for the support of government.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. NEEDS AND BENEFITS: This rule making proposes to adjust the criteria under which non-managing owners of horses in Thoroughbred racing are required to be licensed by the Gaming Commission. Currently, each non-managing owner must be licensed when there are 35 or fewer owners and when an owner has a three percent or more interest, when there are more than 35 owners. This proposal would change those thresholds to, instead, require licensure of each owner only when there are 20 or fewer owners or an owner has a five percent or more interest, when there are more than 20 owners. The five-percent threshold is modeled after the Association of Racing Commissioners International Model Rule and is a standard that many other racing jurisdictions, such as Kentucky, Maryland and Ohio, use. Currently, each non-managing owner must be licensed when there are 35 or fewer owners and when an owner has a three percent or more interest, when there are more than 35 owners.
